arxiv-2108-04701.title: Dust in brown dwarfs and extra-solar planets
arxiv-2108-04701.creator: C. Köhn, Ch. Helling, M. Bødker Enghoff, K. Haynes, D. Krog, J.P. Sindel, D. Gobrecht
arxiv-2108-04701.description: Abstract Context. Modelling the formation of cloud condensation nuclei (CCNs) is key for predicting cloud properties in planet and brown dwarf atmospheres. The large diversity of exoplanets (rocky planets, mini-Neptunes, giant gas planets) requires a fundamental approach to cloud formation modelling in order to allow a full analysis of observational data contributing to exoplanet characterisation. Aims.

arxiv-2201-13101.title: Field theory of structured liquid dielectrics
arxiv-2201-13101.creator: Ralf Blossey, Rudolf Podgornik
arxiv-2201-13101.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ralf Blossey, Rudolf Podgornik. We develop of a field-theoretic approach for the treatment of both the non-local and the non-linear response of structured liquid dielectrics. Our systems of interest are composed of dipolar solvent molecules and simple salt cations and anions. We describe them by two independent order parameters, the polarization field for the solvent and the charge density field for the ions, including and treating the non-electrostatic part of the interactions explicitly and consistently.

arxiv-2301-00089.description: Abstract There are many artificial intelligence algorithms for autonomous driving in the present market, but directly installing these algorithms on vehicles is unrealistic and expensive. arxiv-2507-15685.title: The Win Ratio at the Design Stage of Clinical Trials
arxiv-2507-15685.creator: David Kronthaler, Matthias Schwenkglenks, Felix Beuschlein, Ulrike Held
arxiv-2507-15685.description: Abstract Abstract The win ratio offers a flexible approach to incorporate the hierarchy of clinical outcomes into the analysis of a composite endpoint, enabling simultaneous consideration of multiple outcome types, unlike traditional time-to-first-event (TTFE) analysis or focus on a single outcome.

Alton, Miguel Ángel Álava Amat, Paul Benni, Emmanuel Besson, Patrick Brandebourg, Marc Bretton, Mauro Caló, Martin Valentine Crow
arxiv-2508-15075.description: Abstract We present a comprehensive analysis of transit, eclipse, and radial velocity data of the hot Jupiter TrES-1 b and confirm evidence of orbital variations on secular timescales. Apparent variations due to systemic motion and light travel time effects have been ruled out, indicating that the observed changes are dynamical in origin.

arxiv-2512-14547.title: Lie rings related to the p p -groups of maximal class
arxiv-2512-14547.creator: Bettina Eick, Patali Komma, Subhrajyoti Saha
arxiv-2512-14547.description: Abstract The Lazard correspondence induces a close relation between the p p -groups of maximal class and a certain type of Lie ring constructed from p p -adic number fields. Our aim here is to investigate such Lie rings. In particular, we show that they are always finite. It then follows that they are nilpotent of small class.

arxiv-2602-08032.title: Horizon Imagination: Efficient On-Policy Rollout in Diffusion World Models
arxiv-2602-08032.creator: Lior Cohen, Ofir Nabati, Kaixin Wang, Navdeep Kumar, Shie Mannor
arxiv-2602-08032.description: Abstract We study diffusion-based world models for reinforcement learning, which offer high generative fidelity but face critical efficiency challenges in control. Current methods either require heavyweight models at inference or rely on highly sequential imagination, both of which impose prohibitive computational costs.

pmc-13194334.title: Specialty-based differences in osteoporosis management in Türkiye: a national cross-sectional survey
pmc-13194334.creator: Muhammed Yasir Altunışık, Zekeriya Keskin, Burak Aydın, Musa Polat
pmc-13194334.description: SummaryThis study showed significant specialty-based differences in osteoporosis management in Türkiye. Physical medicine and rehabilitation (PM&R) physicians demonstrated the highest awareness, whereas orthopedic physicians demonstrated the lowest. Guideline use, rather than seniority, was associated with better awareness, supporting targeted education and wider fracture liaison services (FLS) implementation.

pmc-13394769.title: Plant‐protein supplementation improves thermoregulatory responses and ameliorates markers of intestinal damage during exercise in the heat
pmc-13394769.creator: Robyn Aitkenhead, Mark Waldron, Gillian E Conway, Katy Horner, Shane M Heffernan
pmc-13394769.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Exercise in the heat often causes gastrointestinal (GI) disturbances, which can impair performance. Single amino acid supplementation can attenuate gut damage and enhance exercise tolerance; however, the effectiveness of innate amino acid blends from plant‐based proteins remains underexplored. In this study, we investigated the effects of a novel fava bean‐derived plant protein (ATURA) on thermoregulation, endurance performance and GI disturbances during exercise.
